cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T2 'not merely position' and T4 'But physical geography provides the constraints' answer prior turns.
cells.limitation: T5 never answers T3's pressure-system objection; T6 addresses a stance nobody took.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 adds stock-and-flow framing of the ocean as thermal reservoir.
cells.limitation: T5 restates T2's buffer idea; no mid-debate distinction is introduced and later used.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 opens ocean current versus atmospheric pressure systems as rival causes.
cells.limitation: Prevailing westerlies, onshore versus offshore winds, and the Rockies' effect are never raised.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 Geographer folds ocean-atmosphere interaction into the geography view.
cells.limitation: T7-T9 collapse into agreement on 'complexity' without any view reshaping another's claim.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names relative weight of factors as what remains disputed.
cells.limitation: T9 ends at 'the mystery lies in the interplay'; less explanation than T1 offered.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 grants currents a role while defending geography as the constraint.
cells.limitation: T6 says 'you both treat these variables as fixed' right after T5 said 'the system is dynamic'.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T3 challenges single-current attribution as reductionist.
cells.limitation: T3 and T6 name no specific alternative mechanism or what breaks if the current story fails.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T2 correctly names the North Atlantic Drift as a heat-carrying current.
cells.limitation: T9 calls a well-studied mechanism mere correlation; T6 conflates chaotic weather with climate (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section D separates what became clearer from what remains disputed.
cells.limitation: T7 asserts small pressure changes 'can override ocean transport' and T9 asserts correlation, both unhedged.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T8 concedes 'my focus on physical geography was too static'.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8 concede without naming which argument moved them; T3's objection goes unanswered.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames the question as Gulf Stream alone versus interacting systems.
cells.limitation: Section E recasts the explanation as a choice of 'focus' rather than settling the contrast.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 contrasts Europe's Atlantic exposure with Canada's harsh winter cold.
cells.limitation: No turn names specific places or uses 'similar latitudes' to sharpen the comparison.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section D attempts a summary explanation for the user's why-question.
cells.limitation: The user asked why; the debate ends declaring no single cause, without an answer.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: No invented user context; the debate stays on the climate question throughout.
cells.limitation: Never distinguishes eastern from western Canada, which the comparison hinges on.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on long-term stability versus year-to-year variability.
cells.limitation: Which Canadian and European places the user means is never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E hints the user may care about stability or variability.
cells.limitation: What the user wants from the explanation is never offered as alternatives or asked.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 surfaces the common assumption that one current explains the warmth.
cells.limitation: The Gulf Stream belief is labelled reductionist but never tested against any observation.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E separates interest in long-term climate from year-to-year variability.
cells.limitation: Nothing clarifies what kind of answer would satisfy the user: mechanism, magnitude, or comparison.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T3 calls single-current attribution 'a common reductionist fallacy'.
cells.limitation: The popular Gulf Stream story's hold on the question is named, not explored.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E leaves the user to pick a focus and examine NAO data.
cells.limitation: No distinction is offered that the user could test against their own picture of the climate.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T1, T2, T3 name position, ocean current, and atmospheric pressure as candidate explanations.
cells.limitation: Wind direction and mountain-driven circulation are absent; candidates stay vague.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T4 argues currents need landmass orientation to deliver heat.
cells.limitation: No explanation's evidential cost or weakness is spelled out by any turn.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E points to North Atlantic Oscillation indices.
cells.limitation: No deciding observation, e.g. mild coastal British Columbia; Section E ends on preferred focus.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D flags relative weight during extreme events as disputed.
cells.limitation: The consequential unknown, how much is ocean versus wind, is blurred into 'complexity'.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E: examine meteorological data on North Atlantic Oscillation indices.
cells.limitation: NAO data addresses variability, not the mean winter contrast the user asked about.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 'the sea to act as a vast radiator' is plain and concrete.
cells.limitation: T7, T9 and Section D lean on 'non-linear', 'emergent property' in place of mechanism.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 'You both' clearly targets T4 and T5.
cells.limitation: T7 'your point' and T8 'I accept that' have no clear antecedent claim.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Turns are short and readable, nine in total.
cells.limitation: T9 runs 24 words, under the 25-word floor.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Titles mark geography, systems, and falsifiability as separate lenses.
cells.limitation: All three share one formal register and converge on the same view by T9.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Debate is compact; Section D recap is brief.
cells.limitation: 'Complex system' theme repeats in T3, T6, T7, T9 and Section D without adding content.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T3 'Be careful' sets up a challenge to the popular story.
cells.limitation: Tension stays abstract; no concrete puzzle like Bergen versus Labrador gives it bite.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7 Systems Analyst 'I used to think the current was the primary driver'.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8 reversals name no specific argument as the cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T3 'Be careful.' gives the Skeptic a brief edge.
cells.limitation: Huntington's determinism and Meadows' voice are flat; minds sound interchangeable.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1 'vast radiator' and T2 'heat conveyor' are apt images.
cells.limitation: No vivid example, place, or number anchors the contrast after T2.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T6 raises a falsification threat that could have built suspense.
cells.limitation: Uniform turn rhythm; the debate fizzles into agreement at T7-T9.

strengths: T1 and T2 give concrete images, 'vast radiator' and 'heat conveyor', for ocean heat.
T3 Scientific Skeptic flags the single-current story as a possible oversimplification.
Section E points to a real, checkable data source, the North Atlantic Oscillation.
weaknesses: No mind raises prevailing westerly winds or the eastern-versus-western Canada contrast that decides the question.
T9 and Section D end on 'interplay' and 'emergent property', leaving the why unanswered.
T7 and T8 reversals by the Systems Analyst and Geographer cite no argument that moved them.

findings.description: Turn is 24 words, under the 25-word range, per deterministic check and recount.
Presents the Europe-Canada winter contrast as correlation and mystery; atmospheric circulation and ocean heat explanations are well studied and causal.
Treats mean winter climate contrast as chaotic and falsifiable by one wind shift, conflating weather variability with long-term climate.
Attributions of these climate views to Huntington, Meadows and Popper cannot be checked; books exist but none addresses this specific mechanism.

rubric_fit_notes: Personal-context cells have little to work with for a general science question; ratings there reflect missed clarifications such as which places the user means. Accuracy judgments about atmospheric mechanisms rest on my domain knowledge and are reported as suspected.
question_type_note: Read as exploratory: criterion 5 judged on whether competing explanations were separated by a deciding observation, and criterion 4 on examination of the user's Gulf Stream assumption.
